settings.title: Keep it beautiful for decades
settings.text: Solid wood and natural cane age beautifully when cared for properly. These simple habits will keep your furniture looking its best for years to come.

settings.question: Cleaning natural cane webbing
settings.answer: Dust regularly with a soft, dry brush or cloth to stop grit settling into the weave. Twice a year, wipe with a barely-damp cloth and mild soap, then dry immediately. Never soak cane — it can slacken when wet.

settings.question: Caring for the solid wood frame
settings.answer: Wipe with a soft, dry cloth. For deeper cleaning, use a lightly damp cloth and dry straight away. Use coasters and placemats to avoid water rings and heat marks.

settings.question: Maintaining the finish
settings.answer: Our frames are finished with natural, low-VOC oils and waxes. Once or twice a year, apply a thin coat of natural furniture oil or beeswax along the grain, then buff with a soft cloth to restore lustre.

settings.question: Caring for linen and bouclé cushions
settings.answer: Most of our cushion covers are removable and machine-washable on a gentle, cold cycle — check the care label first. Air-dry flat to avoid shrinkage, and fluff cushions regularly to keep their shape.

settings.question: Protecting from sun and heat
settings.answer: Keep furniture out of prolonged direct sunlight, which can fade wood and dry out cane. Avoid placing pieces directly against radiators, heaters or air-conditioning vents.

settings.question: Handling spills and stains
settings.answer: Blot spills immediately with a clean, absorbent cloth — don't rub. For cushions, spot-clean with a mild detergent. For wood, dry the area promptly to prevent water marks.

settings.question: Fixing scratches and marks
settings.answer: Light scratches on wood can often be buffed out with furniture wax. Deeper marks may need a touch of matching wood oil. For cane, a slack panel usually tightens again on its own as the air cools.

settings.question: Cane and humidity
settings.answer: Cane likes a little humidity. In a very dry room it can become brittle over years, so avoid radiators and heating vents. In summer, if a panel slackens slightly, it will usually tighten again as the air cools.
